I agree with defining doxxing as the first step, as well. Originally, doxxing was releasing information used to identify someone in real life. If a hacker had pissed another hacker off, doxxing was a way of releasing personal information in hopes the other guy would be raided, or would at least scare him enough to shut him up. Doxxing nowadays seems to be any and all information about a person, including social media profiles and usernames, etc.

I think we should have two rules when it comes to private information.

1) Doxxing, as in releasing information that was not previously released/provided by the person, or that can link to a person offline, should be off limits.

2) Screen names, link to profiles, or any publicly accessible information, which the person made available to a public audience, should not be considered doxxing and should be fair game. This also shouldn't be used for targeted harassment, but should be used to add context to discussions or at least attribute something to its origin.
